q.q: Complete the sentence with the correct preposition: 'The candidate is eligible ____ the post of TGT Computer Science.'
q.x: The adjective 'eligible' is idiomatically followed by the preposition 'for' when referring to a position or qualification. No other preposition fits the context of job eligibility.

q.q: Choose the correct preposition to complete the sentence: The teacher insisted ____ the students completing the assignment by Friday.
q.x: The verb 'insist' is followed by the preposition 'on'. The construction 'insist on someone doing something' is the standard idiomatic usage.

q.q: Select the appropriate preposition: 'The manager was annoyed ____ the junior developer due to the repeated syntax errors.'
q.x: When one is annoyed with a person, the preposition 'with' is used. If one were annoyed at a situation or an object, 'at' would be appropriate.

q.q: Complete the sentence with the correct conjunction: 'He is intelligent ____ lazy; he rarely completes his assignments on time.'
q.x: The conjunction 'but' is used to connect two clauses that express contrasting ideas. Intelligence and laziness are opposing traits, making 'but' the logical choice.

q.q: You can have tea _____ coffee, but not both.
q.x: The conjunction 'or' is used to show a choice between two alternatives. It signifies that one option excludes the other.

q.q: Select the correct preposition: 'The company aims to provide high-quality software solutions ____ competitive prices.'
q.x: In English, the preposition 'at' is used when referring to prices or rates. 'At competitive prices' is the standard idiomatic expression.

q.q: Select the most appropriate preposition to complete the sentence: 'The committee is divided ____ the issue of mandatory overtime for staff.'
q.x: The preposition 'on' is standard when expressing disagreement or division regarding a specific topic or issue. 'Divided on' implies a difference of opinion, which fits the context perfectly.

q.q: Select the appropriate conjunction: 'Walk carefully ____ you should fall.'
q.x: 'Lest' is a formal conjunction meaning 'for fear that' and is typically followed by 'should'. It is the grammatically correct choice for expressing a warning.

q.q: Identify the appropriate preposition: 'The committee has been debating this issue ____ the last three hours without reaching a consensus.'
q.x: The preposition 'for' is used to denote a duration of time. 'Since' would be used for a specific starting point in the past.

q.q: Identify the correct preposition: The committee has been working ____ the new syllabus for several months.
q.x: The phrasal verb 'work on' means to expend effort on a particular project or task. 'Working on' correctly indicates the focus of the committee's labor.

q.q: Select the correct preposition: 'She jumped _____ the pool to save the drowning child.'
q.x: The preposition 'into' indicates movement from outside to the inside of an enclosed space. 'In' describes the position already inside the space.

q.q: _____ laptop on the desk belongs to the manager.
q.x: The definite article 'the' is used because we are referring to a specific laptop. The context implies a particular object known to the speaker.

q.q: Choose the most appropriate option to complete the sentence: 'She has been working in this organization _____ 2015.'
q.x: The preposition 'since' is used to denote a specific point in time in the past from which an action began and continues to the present. 'For' is used for durations of time, while 'from' typically indicates a starting point but is less idiomatic with present perfect continuous tenses.

q.q: Fill in the blank with the correct article: It is ____ unique opportunity for the students to interact with experts.
q.x: Although 'unique' starts with a vowel letter, it begins with the consonant sound /j/ (yoo-neek). Therefore, the indefinite article 'a' is the correct choice.

q.q: They reached the station _____ time to catch the express train.
q.x: The idiom 'in time' means before it is too late or at the appropriate moment. 'On time' means exactly at the scheduled time.

q.q: It was raining heavily, _____ we decided to stay indoors.
q.x: The conjunction 'so' indicates a consequence or result. It links the cause (heavy rain) to the effect (staying indoors).

q.q: Complete the sentence: 'You can choose either the desktop computer ____ the laptop for your home office setup.'
q.x: The correlative conjunction 'either' is always paired with 'or'. This construction is used to present two mutually exclusive alternatives.

q.q: Pick the correct preposition: 'She has a great deal of affection ____ her students.'
q.x: Affection is generally followed by the preposition 'for' when referring to people. It denotes the feeling directed toward someone.

q.q: She has been waiting for _____ hour to meet the principal.
q.x: We use the indefinite article 'an' before words starting with a vowel sound. Although 'hour' starts with a consonant letter, it begins with a silent 'h' sound.

q.q: Identify the correct conjunction to complete the sentence: '____ had the meeting started when the fire alarm began to ring.'
q.x: The correlative pair 'No sooner... than' is the grammatically correct structure here. 'Scarcely' and 'Hardly' would require 'when', but 'No sooner' is the standard idiomatic choice for this specific sentence structure.

q.q: He is fond _____ playing chess during his lunch break.
q.x: The adjective 'fond' is almost always followed by the preposition 'of'. This is a fixed prepositional phrase in English.

q.q: Identify the error in the sentence: 'Hardly had he stepped out of the office than it started raining.'
q.x: The correlative conjunction 'hardly' must be followed by 'when', not 'than'. 'Than' is used in comparisons or with the word 'scarcely'.

q.q: Identify the correct preposition: The package was delivered ____ the wrong address.
q.x: When referring to a destination or an end point of a delivery, the preposition 'to' is the correct choice. 'At' might indicate location, but 'to' indicates direction or delivery destination.

q.q: Choose the correct article for the blank: 'He is _____ honest man who values integrity above all else.'
q.x: The word 'honest' begins with a silent 'h', resulting in a vowel sound. Therefore, the indefinite article 'an' is the grammatically correct choice.

q.q: Choose the correct article: ____ Ganges is a sacred river in India.
q.x: Definite articles are used before the names of rivers. Therefore, 'The' is required before 'Ganges'.

q.q: Choose the correct article usage: '____ gold is a precious metal, but ____ gold found in this mine is of low quality.'
q.x: General nouns usually don't take an article, so 'gold' (general) takes none. However, 'the gold' is used in the second clause because it refers to a specific quantity of gold in a specific mine.

q.q: The files are kept _____ the top shelf of the cupboard.
q.x: The preposition 'on' is used to indicate a position on a surface. 'On' is correct when referring to items placed upon a shelf.

q.q: Choose the grammatically correct option: 'I bought ____ umbrella from the store, but I lost it the same day.'
q.x: The word 'umbrella' starts with a vowel sound (/ʌ/), so the indefinite article 'an' must precede it. 'A' would be incorrect because it is used before consonant sounds.

q.q: Select the appropriate conjunction to complete the sentence: He had hardly stepped out of the house ____ it began to rain heavily.
q.x: The correlative pair 'hardly... when' is used to indicate that one event happens immediately after another. Using 'than' would be incorrect as it is paired with 'no sooner'.

q.q: The meeting is scheduled _____ 10:00 AM tomorrow.
q.x: The preposition 'at' is used to indicate a precise point in time. It is standard for specific clock times.

q.q: Choose the best option to complete the sentence: 'Neither the manager ____ the employees were aware of the new policy.'
q.x: The correlative conjunction 'neither' must be paired with 'nor'. This pair is used to indicate that both subjects are excluded from the action.

q.q: He is _____ most intelligent student in our computer science batch.
q.x: The definite article 'the' is used before superlative adjectives like 'most intelligent'. It specifies a unique individual within a group.

q.q: Identify the missing conjunction: '____ it was raining heavily, the students reached the exam center on time.'
q.x: The sentence expresses a contrast between the weather and the outcome. 'Although' functions as a subordinating conjunction to introduce this concession.

q.q: Choose the correct preposition to complete the sentence: 'He is proficient _____ solving complex programming problems.'
q.x: The word 'proficient' is followed by the preposition 'at' when referring to a skill or ability. While 'in' is sometimes used, 'at' is the standard preposition for indicating competency in a specific task.

q.q: Choose the correct option to fill in the blank: 'He has been working as ____ SDO in the municipal corporation for over a decade.'
q.x: The abbreviation 'SDO' is pronounced starting with a vowel sound (/es/), which necessitates the indefinite article 'an'. Even though it starts with a consonant letter, the phonetic sound determines the article usage.

q.q: Choose the correct preposition: 'The result of the exam will be declared ____ the second week of June.'
q.x: We use the preposition 'in' for periods of time like weeks, months, or years. 'On' is used for specific dates, and 'at' for precise times.

q.q: Choose the correct article to complete the sentence: 'He is ____ M.A. in English from a reputed university.'
q.x: The abbreviation 'M.A.' starts with a vowel sound (/ɛm/), which requires the indefinite article 'an'. Even though 'M' is a consonant letter, the phonetic sound determines the article usage.

q.q: Fill in the blank with the most suitable conjunction: She was not only tired ____ hungry after the long examination.
q.x: The correlative conjunction 'not only' must be paired with 'but also'. This structure emphasizes that both conditions were true simultaneously.

q.q: Select the correct option: I have been living in this city ____ 2015.
q.x: 'Since' is used to denote a specific point in time in the past from which an action began. 'For' would be used if denoting a duration, such as 'for ten years'.

q.q: Select the correct conjunction to join the clauses: '____ hard he worked, he could not clear the examination.'
q.x: 'No matter how' functions correctly here to introduce a concession. 'Although' would require a different sentence structure, such as 'Although he worked hard'.

q.q: Fill in the blank with the correct article: '_____ Himalayas are known for their majestic peaks.'
q.x: The definite article 'the' is used before the names of mountain ranges. Proper nouns representing geographical regions like mountain chains require 'the'.

q.q: Fill in the blank with the correct article: 'It was ____ unique experience to visit the software laboratory.'
q.x: The word 'unique' begins with a consonant sound (/j/), which is the 'y' sound. Therefore, the indefinite article 'a' is correct instead of 'an'.

q.q: I will complete the project _____ you help me with the data entry.
q.x: The conjunction 'if' is used to introduce a condition. It links the completion of the project to the requirement of assistance.

q.q: Choose the correct article for the sentence: '____ Ganges is considered a sacred river by millions of people in India.'
q.x: Definite articles are used before the names of rivers, mountain ranges, and seas. Therefore, 'The' is required before 'Ganges'.

q.q: Which option correctly completes the sentence: 'I am not interested _____ what he has to say about the project.'
q.x: The adjective 'interested' is conventionally paired with the preposition 'in'. This phrase indicates a lack of engagement or curiosity regarding a specific subject.

q.q: Identify the error-free sentence regarding article usage.
o: He wants to be an astronaut.
The honesty is the best policy.
She plays a guitar very well.
Mount Everest is the highest mountain in a world.
q.x: Option A is correct because 'astronaut' begins with a vowel sound. The others are incorrect: 'honesty' is an abstract noun requiring no article, 'guitar' requires 'the' when referring to musical instruments, and 'the world' is the correct phrasing.

q.q: Select the correct article to fill in the blank: 'It is _____ unique opportunity for the candidates to clear the DSSSB exam.'
q.x: Although 'unique' begins with a vowel letter, it begins with a consonant sound (/j/). Therefore, the article 'a' is required instead of 'an'.

q.q: Complete the sentence with the correct conjunction: '_____ he was ill, he attended the important meeting.'
q.x: The sentence expresses a contrast between being ill and attending a meeting. 'Although' is the correct subordinating conjunction to show this contrast.

q.q: Complete the sentence: 'Not only did he complete the assignment, _____ he also submitted it early.'
q.x: The correlative conjunction pair 'not only... but also' requires the use of 'but' to introduce the second part of the correlation. It emphasizes that both actions occurred.

q.q: Choose the right preposition: 'He is quite adept ____ debugging complex algorithms in Python.'
q.x: The adjective 'adept' is followed by the preposition 'at' when describing proficiency in a specific skill or subject. 'Adept at' implies competence.

q.q: Choose the most appropriate conjunction: You can have either coffee ____ tea, but not both.
q.x: The correlative conjunction 'either' is logically paired with 'or' to present a choice between two alternatives. 'Nor' would only be used if paired with 'neither'.

q.q: Select the appropriate conjunction to fill in the blank: 'You can have either tea _____ coffee.'
q.x: The correlative conjunction 'either' is always paired with 'or' to present a choice between two alternatives. 'Nor' is used with 'neither'.

q.q: Identify the missing preposition: 'The teacher distributed the notes _____ the students.'
q.x: The preposition 'among' is used when distributing something to more than two people. 'Between' is typically reserved for two entities.

q.q: The teacher walked _____ the classroom and started the lecture.
q.x: The preposition 'into' indicates movement from the outside to the inside. It is appropriate when describing entering a physical space.

q.q: Choose the correct conjunction: 'Scarcely had the teacher entered the classroom ____ the students stood up.'
q.x: The correlative structure 'scarcely... when' is used to show one action happening immediately after another. 'No sooner' would be paired with 'than'.

q.q: Fill in the blank: The manager is superior ____ his colleagues in terms of technical experience.
q.x: Adjectives ending in '-ior' such as 'superior', 'inferior', 'senior', and 'junior' take the preposition 'to' instead of 'than' for comparisons. This is a common rule in English grammar.

q.q: Which article correctly completes this sentence? 'It was ____ unique experience working on that distributed systems project.'
q.x: Although 'unique' starts with a vowel, it begins with a consonant sound (/j/). Therefore, the article 'a' is used instead of 'an'.

q.q: She was tired, _____ she continued working on the coding assignment.
q.x: The conjunction 'yet' is used to show a contrast between two ideas. It implies that despite being tired, she persisted.

q.q: Select the correct article: '____ Himalayas are the highest mountain range in the world.'
q.x: Definite article 'the' is used before the names of mountain ranges. Proper nouns like individual peaks do not take an article, but ranges always do.
